results.corrected_title: Microsoft reportedly pulls out as anchor tenant of Nscale's Loughton, Essex data centre ahead of Nscale's IPO
results.corrected_summary: The Telegraph reported on 18 October 2026, and Reuters and others relayed it, that Microsoft has terminated its agreement to be the anchor tenant at Nscale's planned data centre in Loughton, Essex. No reason was given for the withdrawal, and Microsoft did not comment. The site has been delayed repeatedly, and grid officials reportedly told Nscale it should not expect a power connection until the 2030s. Nscale says it remains committed to the site, is looking at alternative power sources, and describes its relationship with Microsoft as 'strong and long-term'. According to Nscale's IPO filing, Microsoft and Anthropic account for about 85% of its contracts.
key_facts: Reported by The Telegraph on Sunday 18 October 2026, relayed by Reuters/Investing.com, TNW and BusinessDay
Microsoft has not commented, and no reason for the withdrawal was given
Grid officials reportedly do not expect a power supply for the site until the 2030s
Nscale is seeking to raise up to $3bn in a US IPO as soon as October 2026; Microsoft and Anthropic make up about 85% of its contracts per the filing
The original plan (announced Sept/Oct 2025) was about 23,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs for Azure from Q1 2027 at a 50 MW site that could be expanded to 90 MW
Nscale's flagship Norway site is about six months behind schedule, with only 6.4 MW of a planned 30 MW running
results.issues: Chip count and delivery date come from the 2025 announcements; present as original plan only. The core withdrawal story rests on a single source (The Telegraph); Microsoft has not confirmed it.

results.corrected_title: Anthropic privately pitches its own draft federal frontier-AI safety bill to US lawmakers, Politico reports
results.corrected_summary: Politico reported on 16 October 2026 that Anthropic has been privately circulating a draft federal bill on frontier AI safety on Capitol Hill. Under the draft, the government could halt a model only if it posed a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damage or more than 50 deaths or serious injuries. The risk would have to come from bioweapons, cyberattacks, or a model evading its developer's controls, and a federal judge in the District of Columbia would have to order any suspension at the Commerce Department's request. Independent evaluators registered with Commerce would assess the labs periodically, and the bill would preempt some state rules on risk disclosure, third-party audits and incident reporting.
key_facts: Original reporting by Politico on 16 Oct 2026; relayed by Bloomberg, Reuters/US News and Business Today
Intervention threshold: imminent risk of more than $1bn in damage or more than 50 people killed or seriously injured
Qualifying risks: biological weapons, cyberattacks, or models evading developer controls
Commerce must ask the US District Court for D.C. to order a suspension; other federal agencies are barred from halting models on their own
Evaluators registered with Commerce would run periodic assessments and must report imminent risks within 72 hours
The bill would preempt some state and local rules on transparency, third-party audits and critical incident reporting
results.issues: The Bloomberg URL returned 403, and the US News page timed out. Details confirmed through Business Today and search summaries of Reuters and Bloomberg. The draft is unpublished and the lawmakers involved were not named.

results.corrected_title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; Disney sets the floor bid at $20 million for a licence to some of its IP
results.corrected_summary: Character Technologies (Character.AI) filed for Chapter 11 in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on 12 October 2026. It cited declining liquidity and the high cost of lawsuits and regulatory investigations into product safety. A Disney entity is the stalking-horse bidder, offering $20 million plus transition support for a non-exclusive, perpetual licence to selected IP and claims. The app, brand, user data, training data and models are excluded. Competing bids are due by 20 November, and the sale is targeted for late November or early December; Disney had already named former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand as its first CTO in September.
key_facts: Chapter 11 filed 12 Oct 2026 in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware
Reasons given: declining liquidity and the cost of litigation and regulatory probes over product safety
Disney is the stalking horse at $20m for a non-exclusive perpetual licence to selected IP and claims; the app, brand, user data and models are excluded
Competing bids are due by 20 Nov; the sale is expected to close in late November or early December
Estimated assets and liabilities are $50m-$100m each
Disney announced Karandeep Anand as CTO on 18 Sept 2026, effective 2 Oct
results.issues: Variety, THR, Benzinga and CNBC pages were blocked. Engadget confirms the $20m stalking-horse bid and the timeline. Court, filing date, licence terms and bid deadline come from search-result summaries of several outlets.
